thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 runtime OOMs on scale-prod-3 (gpu-cluster-2). Triggered by 2212345600 alerts. Symptoms: increased 500s for /v1/generate, per-token failures. Incident channel created: #inc-2212345678.

samir: acknowledging, I'm on it. collecting logs from the affected workers now — tagging @anya for oncall handoff.

anya: taking handoff. current signal: ~12% request failures across the pool, spike started ~10:03 UTC. Pulling nvidia and cgroup stats. Can we mute non-prod to reduce noise?

oncall-bot: muted channel for non-prod alerts.

devon: pasting a cropped nvidia-smi snapshot from one affected host:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB  Memory-Usage: 36784MiB / 40960MiB (free: 4180MiB)
| Processes: 1 python(36650MiB), 1 cudaDriver(30MiB)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Fragmentation heuristic: free large contiguous blocks < required allocation (1.2GiB) -> alloc fail
```

maria: ping — any visible customer impact beyond error spike? which teams/customers hit?

devon: initial blast affected 4 ML-serving clusters, ~25 pods across 6 nodes. Customer-facing latencies spiked and some requests returned 500 with "cuda runtime error: out of memory". CS reported 3 customers saw degraded experience.

samir: live mitigation proposals (short list): 1) reduce batch_size from 8 -> 4 on hot routes; 2) increase kv-cache eviction aggressiveness; 3) route some traffic to smaller model variant (fp16->int8) as fallback; 4) node drain for deep investigation if still unstable. Which can we push without heavy churn?

anya: we can do 1+2 immediately. i'll push a hot-config to change `BATCH_SIZE` env and `KV_CACHE.max_entries` via console. prepping rollout to 10% then 100% if stable. also open to model fallback but prefer config first.

devon: applied quick fixes: `kubectl set env deploy/model-worker BATCH_SIZE=4 --record` and `rkctl kvcache update --max-entries 1000 --eviction-policy lru` on the affected pool. restarted 6 pods (rolling).

samir: please paste the exact commands and logs you ran so we can capture timeline.

devon: commands run:```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/model-worker-variantA
rkctl kvcache update --pool scale-prod-3 --max-entries=1000 --eviction=lru
# verified via: rkctl kvcache stats --pool scale-prod-3
```
logs snippet:```
[10:08:12] worker-7 ERROR gpu_alloc failed: required=1.2GiB free_contig=800MiB -> cuda OOM
[10:09:01] control INFO kvcache eviction triggered, evicted 1200 entries
[10:09:40] worker-3 INFO batch_size reduced to 4
```

maria: early customer-impact update: error rate dropped from 12% -> ~2% within 4m after the rollout. CS notified affected customers and asked for postmortem.

anya: building a minimal timeline for RCA:
- 10:03 UTC: first OOM alerts (scale-prod-3)
- 10:05 UTC: incident auto-opened by pager
- 10:06 UTC: initial oncall ack (samir)
- 10:08 UTC: repeated cuda OOM logs across pods
- 10:09 UTC: applied batch_size reduction + kvcache eviction config
- 10:13 UTC: observed error rate drop to ~2%

samir: let's enumerate hypotheses (we'll mark them and track evidence):
H1: KV cache growth + stale eviction config -> memory pressure and fragmentation (evidence: large eviction event at 10:09).
H2: Batch-size regression in recent deploy increased per-request allocation (evidence: reproducer shows higher peak allocations after deploy at 09:55).
H3: GPU memory fragmentation (allocator can't satisfy contiguous huge allocs even though free total seems adequate).
H4: Driver/CUDA change or kernel-level page fragmentation after host patch.

devon: collecting additional artifacts: `dmesg` shows repeated "Out of memory: Killed process" for a python worker on one host; also capturing per-pod `malloc_stats` and `cudaMalloc` fail traces. uploading to /shared/incidents/2212345678/logs.tar.gz (link: https://files.redwood.internal/incidents/2212345678/logs.tar.gz).

anya: action items during live:
- devon: capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` dumps for all affected nodes (assigned).
- samir: diff the commit between last good deploy and current for batch codepaths (assigned).
- infra: check host-level page reclaim and kernel updates (anya).
- biz: CS to notify customers and collate impacted accounts (maria).

maria: shared list of affected customers in the doc (link): https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/2212345678/customers. CS requested estimated MTTR explanation for exec.

devon: quick note from low-level traces: we see many small KV cache allocations pinned in GPU memory; eviction didn't free contiguous blocks quickly enough, leading to fragmentation. Also a worker was trying to allocate a contiguous tensor of ~1.2GiB which failed despite ~4GiB total free (fragmented).

samir: interim conclusion for live ops: combination of H1 + H3 most likely. Mitigations worked (batch down + kv eviction) and should remain until RCA completes. No immediate need to roll back code yet.

anya: next steps for RCA: snapshot allocator internals, capture a reproducer with script that simulates high kv-cache warmup and large single-tensor allocations, and run on staging with slab debug flags. scheduling a post-incident RCA meeting in 24h.

devon: created follow-up tickets: INC-2212345678-1 (kv-eviction-bug), INC-2212345678-2 (allocator-telemetry), INC-2212345678-3 (batch-regression-bisect). Links in thread.

oncall-bot: noted update: severity downgraded to P2 at 10:45 UTC; monitoring for 2h.

maria: CS confirmed customers acknowledged the interim workaround; asked for ETA on permanent fix.

samir: owners for full RCA: devon (runtime), anya (infra). Expected RCA doc within 24h and a remediation PR for eviction tuning and telemetry within 48h.

anya: uploading collected artifacts to the incident folder now. please avoid changes to the pool until we snapshot.

devon: copied final log dump and heap snapshots to the shared location (same link). I'll also attach `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE` outputs.

samir: thanks everyone. closing live mitigation coordination thread — moving to RCA doc for deep analysis. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updates will be posted to #inc-2212345678 and the docket.```
